key_messages: Near record high temperatures are expected on Wednesday with mostly sunny conditions and some localized fire weather concerns.
A weak cold front will produce scattered showers on Thursday, but precipitation amounts will be light with highest amounts in the mountains.
Repeated chances for showers this weekend and early next week with temperatures gradually decreasing towards seasonal levels.

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Burlington VT
206 PM EST Tue Nov 3 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
As of 204 PM EST Tuesday...

No significant changes made.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
As of 204 PM EST Tuesday...

1. Near record high temperatures are expected on Wednesday with 
mostly sunny conditions and some localized fire weather concerns.

2. A weak cold front will produce scattered showers on 
Thursday, but precipitation amounts will be light with highest 
amounts in the mountains. 
  

3. Repeated chances for showers this weekend and early next 
week with temperatures gradually decreasing towards seasonal levels.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
As of 204 PM EST Tuesday...

KEY MESSAGE 1: Sfc analysis shows a warm frnt draped along the 
International Border this aftn with some scattered rain showers acrs 
northern NY into central/northern VT. Rainfall amounts have been 
<0.10" thru 2 PM. Warm frnt wl lift north of cwa this evening with 
latest RAP ua showing building mid/upper lvl ridge over the Ohio 
Valley into western PA. GOES-19 mid lvl water vapor imagery
indicates well defined dry slot with strong subsidence, which 
is progged to be acrs our fa on Weds, resulting in partly to 
mostly sunny skies. This combined with progged 925mb temps btwn 
15-18C with south/southwest downslope flow wl support highs 
upper 60s to mid 70s with a few warmer valleys reaching the 
upper 70s possible. The localized fire weather concerns would be
acrs the Champlain Valley and northern slopes of the Dacks, 
where gusts of 15 to 20 mph and minimal humidity values will 
drop btwn 35 and 45%. Elsewhere, winds will be lighter east of 
the Green and humidities slightly higher. 

A very warm night is anticipated on Weds night, with southerly flow 
and increasing clouds ahead of our approaching cold frnt. Based on 
sounding analysis feel some deeper/protected valleys east of the 
Greens may decouple, resulting in localized cooler spots and 
supporting a wide range in temps. Similar type idea is anticipated 
in the valleys of the dacks too. Lows generally in the upper 30s to 
mid/upper 50s, warmest in the CPV and downslope areas of the 
northern Dacks near Malone. 925mb winds increase 25-35 knots 
overnight with some localized gusts in the trrn up to 40 mph 
possible. Still some uncertainty on mixing profiles over the cooler 
Lake Champlain waters on Weds night into Thurs for the potential 
need of a lake wind advisory. Sounding data at CLCR is very stable 
in the bl over the cooler lake waters, resulting in minimal mixing 
of stronger winds to the sfc.

KEY MESSAGE 2: Mid/upper lvl trof wl be weakening acrs the 
Midwest/western Great Lakes on Thurs, while pre-frontal trof and 
associated narrow axis of 700-500mb moisture moves from west to east 
acrs our cwa. Given the dampening upper lvl dynamics and out of 
phased energy, feel this precip on Thurs wl be another high pops/low 
qpf event. In addition, developing southwest flow of 35 to 45 knots 
wl produce localized downslope shadowing acrs the CPV, which is 
highlighted nicely in the latest GFS precip fields. Pw values with 
deep southwest flow surge btwn 1.0 to 1.4" ahead of dampening trof 
on Thurs, which are 3 to 4 STD above normal, so thinking everybody 
should at least measure precip. QPF amounts wl range from a few 
hundredths to a quarter inch over the dacks/parts of the SLV. 
Progged 925mb temps btwn 14-12C with more clouds support highs upper 
50s to mid/upper 60s depending upon elevation. Thursday night into 
Friday is relatively quiet with slowly cooling thermal profiles, 
supporting highs in the mid 50s to mid 60s on Friday, which is 5 to 
10 degrees above normal for early Nov. The cooler weather, higher 
humidities and some precipitation wl help mitigating the fire wx 
concerns.

KEY MESSAGE 3: Multi-level closed low pressure over the Great Lakes and 
surface low pressure driving northward along the Northeast Coast 
this weekend will bring increased chances for precipitation, about 
45-75% in Vermont and 25-55% across northern New York Friday night. 
Nighttime temperatures will remain well above seasonal normals with 
projected lows in the mid 30s to mid 40s with plenty of cloud cover 
around. Chances for precipitation decrease on Saturday as surface 
forcing pulls northeastward away from the area, but rain shower 
chances still remain around 35-65% throughout the day as upper level 
troughing stalls overhead. Temperatures will continue to be warmer 
than normal values, but should feel cool compared to the week's 
record warmth. Highs Saturday are expected to be only in the 50s and 
lower 60s. Upper low pressure will head away from the region 
Saturday night, lowering precip chances on Saturday night, and to 
follow Sunday daytime chances decrease further in brief weak 
ridging. Low temperatures during this period are expected to fall 
each night, from the 30s and lower 40s Saturday night down to the 
20s and lower 30s early next week, which could mean snow mixing in 
with the rain at higher elevations and colder spots. Highs will also 
follow a decreasing trend, though more gradual, with temperatures 
hitting the mid 40s and 50s each afternoon through early next week 
and shower chances each day under cyclonic flow.

&&

.AVIATION /18Z TUESDAY THROUGH SUNDAY/...
Through 18Z Wednesday...Light rain showers continue this 
afternoon and evening, primarily north of site KRUT. VFR will 
prevail throughout much of the TAF period, although ceilings are
expected to lower over the next few hours, resulting in some 
sites seeing MVFR level cigs and visibilities in showers. 
Showers will wind down by roughly 00Z-04Z Wednesday. Widespread
VFR conditions anticipated to return around 00Z-08Z Wednesday. 
Breezes will be southerly and southwesterly tonight and tomorrow
and are expected to increase, gusting 15-20 knots in the 
Champlain Valley by 00Z Wednesday. A low level jet out of the 
southwest and west 30-35 knots is likely to cause some LLWS at 
the New York sites around 22Z Tuesday onwards.

Outlook...

Wednesday Night: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Thursday: Mainly MVFR, with areas VFR possible. Chance SHRA.
Thursday Night: Mainly VFR, with local MVFR possible. Chance
SHRA.
Friday: VFR. Chance RA.
Friday Night: MVFR. Chance RA.
Saturday: Mainly MVFR, with areas IFR possible. Chance RA.
Saturday Night: MVFR. Chance RA.
Sunday: Mainly MVFR, with areas IFR possible. Slight chance RA.

&&
